STATUS: BUILD STOPPED. Do not launch. The binding spec contradicts itself in one place, and the selftest fails on it by design.

THE CONTRADICTION (blocking). The execution note gives a formula and a planted answer for the per-atom step rate, and they disagree.
- The formula (checklist item 6) is: atoms x ns_per_day x 1e-9 / (timestep_fs x 1e-15) / 86,400.
- The planted check for the fifth endpoint's instrument (checklist item 9, case I7) expects: 11,250 atoms at 200 ns/day and 2 fs gives 1.3021e10.
- The formula gives 13,020,833 atom-steps per second, which is 1.3021e7. The planted value is 1,000 times larger.
- Independent check: 200 ns/day at 2 fs is 1e8 steps per day, so 1,157.4 steps per second. Times 11,250 atoms gives 1.3021e7.
- I implemented both exactly as written and changed neither. A human must say which one binds. After that, one line changes (run_m3.py line 907 or line 1989).

WHAT IT DOES. It has the three stages the task names, each runnable on its own: extract, generate and endpoints. It also has a cost and time check (guard), summary, void and --selftest.
- Records go through frozen/provenance.py: one per endpoint, ten in all, with the throughput claim, gate and re-pricing as separate records.
- There is one record for the timed dry run, one for each of the ten instrument checks, one per simulation run, and one each for the graphics-card package check and the deck edits.
- Every record, and every raw row, carries run_valid. That includes the per-run files and the raw rows of each simulation run and each thermo line.
- A failed gate or anchor writes run_valid=false into RUN_VALID.json, so every later record and row carries false.

FOUR READINGS THAT NEED A RULING (I chose one; none is a patch).
1. Sanity check text match. The literal text 'SHAKE' appears in LAMMPS's routine line 'Finding SHAKE clusters ...', which is printed before every run. Read across a whole log, the match would fail every run. That would force the throughput claim to be unread. I applied the four text matches only to each 200 ps run's own output, from its thermo header through its 'Loop time' line.
2. Pre-launch build gate on the box. The launcher's payload does not ship out/, which holds the builder's exit code and the CPU zero-step read_data log. On the box this gate checks the parts present: net charge 0.0 and 11,250 atoms. Its decision reads PASS_ON_PARTS_PRESENT. Run locally, it reads the full record.
3. Dry-run wall-clock. Date stamps bracket the 1,000 timed steps, written by a LAMMPS 'shell date' command. The timed run uses 'run 1000 pre no', so set-up is not inside the bracket.
4. Edit 2 (no per-step sampling). It also deletes 'variable dump_every'. Only the two deleted sampling commands use that variable, so it 'exists only for sampling'.

OTHER BUILD CHOICES.
- A stage that stops the run, or a stop by the cost or time guard, also sets run_valid=false. The spec named only gates, the anchor and the install.
- The guard's estimate numbers are mine, not the design's: a 1.25 margin, 60 s per engine stage, 120 s kept free, 600 s billed outside the run, and 100 ns/day before any speed is measured.
- No dispersion rule exists in the design, so no zero-dispersion case was planted.

It follows the note's order on the box. It never runs locally; only a syntax check ran here (bash -n).
1. A cost and time check runs first.
2. Install: it downloads micromamba 2.9.0 and records its sha256. It also checks that hash against the value the coolant pilot measured for the same file.
3. It creates ./engine with 'lammps=2024.08.29=cuda126_py310_h894d002_nompi_2'. If that fails, it uses 'lammps=2024.08.29=cuda126_py310*nompi*'.
4. It sets CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA from nvidia-smi. It saves the install log, both micromamba listings and the lmp -h output under results_m3/out/.
5. Then come the GPU package check, the dry run, the box copy, the equilibration, runs a, b and c, and the endpoints. Each stage runs its own guard first.

Following the execution note, there is no Python environment, no pip and no apt. The task's generic template said 'venv', but the note forbids it.
- An install failure gives code 2 and run_valid=false, and the summary is still written.
- Any nonzero stage code voids the run, writes the summary, writes RUN_DONE with the code, and exits with it.
- An unexpected exit does the same through an exit trap.
- It exports its own process id, so the guard can read how much of the 5,400-second window is left.
- The run stops cleanly before projected spend reaches BUDGET_LEFT_USD. Under time pressure it cuts run c first, then run b.

built.expected:
These are expectations for the run once it is allowed. The build is currently stopped.

WALL-CLOCK
- The hard cap is 5,400 s on the box. That is USD 2.985 at USD 1.99 per hour, under the USD 5 per-launch budget.
- The engine steps are fixed: 500,000 for equilibration, plus at most 10,000 minimiser evaluations, and 125,000 for each production run (warm-up plus 200 ps).
- At the card's 250 ns/day (1,446.76 steps per second), equilibration takes about 346 s and each production run about 86 s, plus engine start-up.
- Run a, the deck as written, is expected to be the slowest of the three runs because of its per-step sampling.
- Install time is unknown: the conda-forge download speed has not been measured. The guard bounds it.

FILES IN results_m3/out/
- 29 record files:
  - 10 endpoint records: the throughput claim, gate and re-pricing are separate.
  - 13 control records: the timed dry run, ten instrument checks, the graphics-card package check and the deck edits.
  - 6 run records: dry run, box copy, equilibration, runs a, b and c.
- raw_runs.jsonl: 5 rows, one per simulation run.
- raw_thermo.jsonl: about 191 rows: 4 from the dry run, about 106 from equilibration (the minimiser block varies), and 27 from each production run.
- guard_rows.jsonl: 9 rows, one per stage.
- Plus RUN_VALID.json, stages.json, labels.json, env.txt, m3_summary.json and RUN_DONE.
- Plus every LAMMPS log and screen capture, the density file, the dry-run date stamps, the install record and log, both micromamba listings, lmp -h and nvidia-smi output.
- Plus the edited decks with their diffs, under decks/.

SAMPLE FILES
- Only the first and last 5 lines of the sample files come back. Row counts are recorded in the run records and the throughput endpoint records.
- Run a writes both files; run b writes the pressure file only; run c writes neither.
- The note expects 20,000 rows each for run a. LAMMPS usually also writes step 0, so 20,001 would not be an error. The count is recorded, not judged.

NOT YET VERIFIED
- Whether the GPU package accepts the equilibration deck's tiled communication and load-balancing commands. Any such error stops the run with code 12.
